However, the summit's expected yield is symbolic: analysts across Chatham House, CSIS, CFR, and CNBC uniformly flag limited breakthroughs on Iran, with a tariff truce more likely than a deal-enabling Xi message to Tehran. No US counter-counter-offer to Iran was issued on May 13. The deal track remains structurally in the same near-terminal condition it was in on May 12 — Trump's '1% chance' framing has not been retracted; the military action lean confirmed by two Axios officials has not been walked back; new Iran sanctions unveiled May 12 remain operative. On the domestic clock: Warsh Fed chair vote is expected Wednesday May 14 (1 day); Powell expiry is May 15 (2 days); Reconciliation 2.0 Finance committee text remains unreleased with the May 15 committee submission deadline now 2 days away. vibe.rationale: Vibe holds at 2 — unchanged from May 12 evening. The Trump-Xi Beijing summit is the one new structural input that prevents a further drop toward 1, but it is insufficient to move the needle upward. The argument for staying at 2 rather than recovering to 3: the underlying deal-track deterioration from May 12 is fully intact on May 13. No counter-counter-offer has been issued. Trump's '1% chance' framing — the most terminal presidential language applied to the deal track since negotiations began — has not been retracted or modified. The two-official Axios confirmation of Trump leaning toward military action has not been walked back. New Iran sanctions unveiled May 12 are now 24 hours old and unreversed. Iran's 'never bow' posture is unchanged. Oil closed at its highest level since Project Freedom launched ($107.77 Brent, $102.18 WTI) — meaning the market's war risk premium has not eased one cent since the May 12 deterioration. The argument against dropping to 1: Trump being physically in Beijing is a meaningful signal that he is engaged in diplomacy rather than issuing a resumption order. The Trump-Xi summit creates a 48-72 hour natural window during which military action is structurally less likely — it would be diplomatically incoherent to launch strikes while the president is in Beijing meeting the leader of Iran's most significant external partner. China's leverage over Iran is real, even if the summit's expected outcome is limited. Xi has an interest in Hormuz reopening that runs deeper than Pakistan or Qatar's interests. The summit produces a new escalation-inhibiting context that did not exist on May 12. Vibe 2: deal near-terminal, Beijing summit creates inhibiting window but no deal-positive signal, military action lean unchanged, oil at crisis-level close, Finance text absent with 2 days to deadline, WPA Day 14.

items.headline: Trump in Beijing for Trump-Xi Summit (May 12-15); Iran War Dominant Agenda Item; Xi as First Genuinely Leveraged Intermediary Since Pakistan/Qatar Channels Went Empty; Symbolic Outcome Expected
items.summary: President Trump arrived in Beijing for the Trump-Xi summit — his first visit to China since 2017 and his first face-to-face with Xi Jinping since October 2025. The summit was originally scheduled for early April but was postponed due to the Iran war; the war now dominates the agenda, leaving trade, tariffs, and Taiwan as secondary items. Trump's delegation enters Beijing seeking Xi's use of Chinese leverage to pressure Iran into reopening the Strait of Hormuz and accepting US nuclear conditions. China has relationships with both Iran and the Gulf states that no other intermediary currently active in the process (Pakistan, Qatar) can match. CNBC, CSIS, Chatham House, and CFR analysts uniformly project limited near-term breakthroughs on Iran: China's leverage is real but Xi is unlikely to deliver a binding Tehran commitment in a first-round summit session. On trade, a tariff truce — not structural change — is the expected output. Trump downplayed US-Iran differences before departing for Beijing, which is either a genuine signal of diplomatic flexibility or a traveling posture. Trump's physical presence in Beijing creates a 48-72 hour window during which resumed military action against Iran would be structurally incoherent — it would be diplomatically impossible to order Project Freedom resumption while the president is sitting with the leader of Iran's most significant external partner. That inhibiting effect is real, but it is a timing constraint, not a deal advance. The key signal to watch is any Trump-Xi joint statement language on the Hormuz crisis, any Xi commitment to engage Tehran directly, or any modification to Trump's '1% chance' framing in the context of Beijing meetings Thursday-Friday.

metrics.analyst_consensus_summit_outcome: symbolic — limited Iran breakthrough, tariff truce more likely

items.headline: Project Freedom Pause Day 8: No Resumption Order; No US Counter-Counter-Offer; Deal Track Near-Terminal; War Cost $29B; Gulf Drone/Naval Incident Ledger Unresolved
items.summary: Project Freedom Pause Day 8 (May 13) ended without a resumption order and without a US counter-counter-offer to Iran's May 8 formal proposal. The deal track's structural condition is unchanged from May 12 evening: Trump has publicly given it a 1% chance of survival; two Axios-confirmed officials stated he is leaning toward military action; new sanctions unveiled May 12 operationalize the coercive track; Iran is locked into 'never bow' posture with no formal mechanism for retreat. The Pentagon confirmed Tuesday that cumulative US war costs have reached $29 billion — a cost figure that will inform both congressional budget arguments and Trump's own political calculus as Reconciliation 2.0 negotiations proceed simultaneously. The unresolved accumulated incident ledger from the pause period remains intact: the May 9 Saturday naval exchange, and Monday's three-country drone cluster (UAE, Qatar, Kuwait) — CENTCOM has issued no public statement on either set of incidents. The inhibiting effect of the Beijing summit does not erase these unanswered incidents from the escalation ledger; it merely defers any administration response. Pakistan and Qatar intermediary channels have not been formally terminated but remain functionally empty: the president's own '1% chance' framing leaves no US negotiating position for intermediaries to transmit. The deal is structurally dead absent an explicit Trump reversal.

items.headline: Oil at Post-Launch High: Brent $107.77 / WTI $102.18 (May 12 Close); WTI Above $100 for First Sustained Session; EIA $115 Q2 Peak Trajectory; Beijing Summit Cannot Directly Reopen Hormuz
items.summary: Oil markets closed May 12 at their highest levels since Project Freedom launched on May 4: Brent crude at $107.77/barrel (+3.4% session gain) and WTI at $102.18/barrel (+4.2%). WTI's breach of $100 — sustained through Tuesday's session — is the first time the US benchmark has held above that level since the oil shock's peak in late April. The EIA's Q2 2026 Brent peak scenario of $115/barrel is now approximately $7 away; at the current trajectory and given the absence of any deal-positive signal through May 13, the scenario is directionally operative. The Trump-Xi Beijing summit creates a secondary oil-market variable: any signal from Beijing that China will actively pressure Iran toward Hormuz reopening would produce an immediate downward crude response, as China's leverage is qualitatively different from Pakistan's or Qatar's. However, no Xi commitment to Tehran engagement has been confirmed as of May 13 evening, and analyst consensus projects a symbolic summit outcome. Saudi Aramco CEO Amin Nasser has confirmed that the market faces a rebalancing delay until 2027 if Hormuz remains blocked past mid-June — approximately 4 weeks from today. National average US gasoline prices remain above $4.50/gallon (AAA) with Portland-area regular above $5.00; the May 12 Brent close ensures no consumer-level relief for at least 2-4 additional weeks. Every day of Hormuz closure is approximately 14-16 million barrels of lost supply.

items.headline: Warsh Chair Vote Wednesday (1 Day); Powell Expiry May 15 (2 Days); Reconciliation Finance Text Absent With 2 Days to Deadline; Trump-Xi Tariff Truce Expected
items.summary: Kevin Warsh was confirmed as a Federal Reserve Board of Governors member on May 12 by a 51-45 Senate vote, with Senator John Fetterman (D-PA) the sole Democratic crossover. The separate Senate vote to designate Warsh as Fed Chair is now expected Wednesday May 14 — one day from this brief — ahead of Jerome Powell's term expiry on May 15. If the Chair vote proceeds as scheduled Wednesday, Warsh will become the nation's central banker on the same day that Senate committees face their Reconciliation 2.0 submission deadline. Warsh's monetary inheritance has not improved since May 12: Brent closed $107.77 on Tuesday, his first day as a confirmed Board governor, and he assumes the chairship in a posture where the primary economic shock — Hormuz supply disruption — is immune to interest-rate tools. His first FOMC meeting (expected June 16) will occur either in the aftermath of resumed Project Freedom military operations or in the improbable scenario of a Beijing-catalyzed deal reversal. Reconciliation 2.0: the May 15 committee submission deadline is now 2 days away. The Senate Finance Committee has not released its text for the tax provisions — the most politically sensitive element of the bill and the one most likely to generate Republican defections. DHS/Judiciary $72B has been CBO-scored and is cleared; the Finance gap is the primary legislative risk. Trump-Xi summit: a tariff truce — not structural change — is the expected trade outcome. A truce would ease secondary market uncertainty but would not offset the oil shock, which is unrelated to tariff architecture.

items.headline: CISA Day 10: Clean Streak Intact; Beijing Summit Marginally Inhibits IRGC Cyber Pre-Positioning Window; 72-Hour Reset Watch Still Operative; No Updated Advisory
items.summary: Ten days after Project Freedom launched on May 4, the United States has sustained no confirmed IRGC-affiliated destructive cyberattack on critical infrastructure. The clean streak remains the most significant positive signal in the current environment and enters Day 10 under marginal structural improvement from one new factor: Trump's physical presence in Beijing for the Trump-Xi summit reduces the near-term probability of a US military strike order against Iran, which in turn marginally reduces the IRGC's incentive to pre-position cyber capabilities for an immediate retaliatory response. The IRGC's cyber retaliation doctrine is most acutely triggered by imminent or actual US kinetic escalation — and a presidential summit in Beijing with Iran's most significant external partner constitutes a credible 48-72 hour escalation-inhibiting context. This is a marginal improvement in the cyber risk environment, not a structural one: the underlying risk drivers from May 12 remain intact. Trump's '1% chance' framing eliminates the diplomatic restraint incentive; new sanctions operationalize coercive pressure; and two officials have confirmed the military action lean. The 72-hour priority watch window from Monday May 11 has expired; but the accumulated reset-triggering events from May 12 (Trump '1% chance' + new sanctions) continue to sustain an elevated baseline alert posture. No updated CISA emergency directive, FBI/IC3 flash, or private-sector OT/ICS alert has been issued. CISA AA26-097A (April 7) remains operative. CI Fortify remains active across energy, water, and government facility sectors. FINRA financial-sector alert and NERC grid monitoring remain live.

items.headline: BLM Campfire Restrictions Effective May 13 Central Oregon; Full OR/WA BLM Fire Restrictions Begin May 14; Oregon Fire Season Day 6 Quiet; 19 Days to East Cascades Above-Normal Onset
items.summary: Oregon's wildfire season entered Day 6 (May 13) with two new operational markers: annual campfire restrictions took effect May 13 on BLM-managed rivers in Central Oregon, and the Bureau of Land Management announced full fire restrictions across Oregon and Washington beginning May 14. The progressive restriction tightening is consistent with the structural risk calendar — the above-normal fire risk onset for east of the Cascades is 19 days away (June 1), and the pre-positioning window for federal and state resources is narrowing. No NWS red flag warning was issued for Oregon or Washington on May 13; no active fire ignitions of significance were reported in either state. Statewide ODF permit restrictions remain in effect; Portland metro and BLM Oregon-Washington burn bans remain active; Washington DNR restrictions continue. The federal capacity gap raised by Oregon's congressional Democrats (May 7) — specifically DOGE-related Forest Service Region 6 fire science research and pre-positioning position eliminations — remains formally unaddressed by USDA or Interior as of Tuesday evening. National wildfire acreage burned YTD remains approximately 1.85 million acres — nearly double the 10-year average for this date. The escalating restriction timeline (May 13 campfires, May 14 full BLM restrictions, June 1 above-normal onset) leaves 19 days of resource pre-positioning time against a structurally certain above-normal season.

items.headline: WPA Day 14: Beijing Defers But Does Not Resolve Resumption; Warsh Chair Vote 1 Day; Powell Expiry 2 Days; Finance Text Absent With 2 Days to Deadline
items.summary: May 13 is WPA Day 14 past the April 29 statutory deadline — the deepest unauthorized war-operation run since the modern War Powers Resolution's enactment. Trump's presence in Beijing for the Trump-Xi summit creates a natural 48-72 hour deferral on any Project Freedom resumption order, but it does not resolve the WPA structural gap: if Trump returns from Beijing and orders resumption before Congress acts, the operation would resume in an equally unauthorized posture. Senate Republicans have defeated six Democratic war-powers resolutions; no seventh has been scheduled. The Trump administration's operative legal interpretation — that the WPA clock stopped when hostilities were 'effectively ended' — remains unlitigated and now structurally inverted: the president publicly gives the ceasefire a 1% survival chance, confirming hostilities are not effectively over. Domestic convergence: Warsh Fed chair vote is expected Wednesday May 14 (1 day), removing the second element of the triple-convergence cluster that opened the week; Powell's 8-year term expires Friday May 15 (2 days). Reconciliation 2.0: the May 15 committee submission deadline is 2 days away. The Senate Finance Committee has not released committee text for the tax and revenue provisions — the most politically volatile and largest single outstanding element. DHS/Judiciary $72B is CBO-scored and cleared. If Finance cannot deliver text by May 15, the Reconciliation 2.0 committee deadline will be missed, creating the first concrete evidence that Trump's June 1 completion target is at risk. No Finance committee public signal of imminent text release was reported as of May 13 evening.

items.headline: OHA Measles Update Due Wednesday; First Hospitalization Day 1 Follow-Up; Last Published Count ~20 (April 22); Wastewater Active; School Window ~2.5 Weeks; CDC National Count Stale
items.summary: Oregon Health Authority confirmed the state's first measles hospitalization of 2026 on Tuesday May 12 — the most significant single Oregon outbreak event since the initial outbreak declaration. OHA's next case count update is expected Wednesday May 14; the hospitalization is likely to prompt OHA to issue an updated count given the elevated public profile of the severity event. The last published Oregon confirmed case count (~20 as of April 22) is now 21 days stale; active wastewater detections across multiple counties and the first-household spread to a multi-household outbreak in Multnomah and Clackamas counties suggest the actual case count is materially higher. Of the last published 20 cases, 19 involved unvaccinated individuals or those with unknown vaccination status — the structural transmission driver. Washington State remains at 40+ confirmed cases across 8 counties, with Kittitas County in active outbreak status. The national CDC confirmed case count was 1,842 as of May 7 (7 days stale); the next CDC update is overdue. The PNW school-year vaccination catch-up window has narrowed to approximately 2.5 weeks (most PNW school districts close mid-to-late June 2026). The hospitalization is the primary Oregon public health watch item going into Wednesday: it changes the response urgency calculus for OHA and raises the probability of an emergency briefing or updated county-level guidance. The discharged patient reportedly is recovering.
